detect-names-and-quotes-no-score:
Reads strongly as machine-made. Almost every clause is a tell, several stacked in one sentence.

- "In today's fast-paced digital landscape" — stock throat-clearing opener (A4/banned openers).
- "isn't just a tool - it's a partner" — not-X-but-Y staging (A1), plus an em dash used as a connector (C5).
- "stands as a testament to" — avoids the plain verb and inflates significance at once (B7, B1).
- "pivotal" — AI-vocabulary flag word (GPT-4/4o era).
- "seamless" — another AI-vocabulary flag word.
- "vibrant" — sales-language inflation (B4), odd applied to "collaboration" rather than a place.
- "empowering teams to unlock their full potential" — vague declarative with no checkable content (B2); "empowering" and "unlock potential" are both stock AI/corporate phrasing.

What's missing is as telling as what's there: no specific feature, no concrete claim, nothing a reader could act on or verify. The whole sentence could be pasted into any SaaS homepage unchanged, which is itself the signature of the "widest range of readers" default this skill is built to catch.

Nothing here reads as a person — no odd specific, no real stance, no uneven rhythm.

Dan
